## TL;DR

Improved first-load placeholders for Mission Control and Stories and audited the other page skeleton kinds. Mission Control now uses one calm dashboard block, Settings keeps a representative set of grouped rows, and the named count constants document the layouts each shape represents. The shell delay and minimum-visible timing remain centralized. The shell and route switch through a short out-in opacity transition, with the animation disabled for reduced motion. The final scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

The original dashboard skeleton used a board-like grid that broke into multiple rows at wide widths and did not resemble Mission Control. Mission Control is a stacked dashboard of panels, so its accepted skeleton is one full-width block. Stories uses a row-oriented layout. The skeleton count mapping in `loading-skeleton.ts` names the representative count for each kind and comments which real layout it mirrors; `PageSkeleton` uses that mapping. The Settings shape remains multiple rows because Settings is a long list of grouped options, while the other shapes use the agreed minimal representative counts.

Loading timing remains owned by the application shell: it delays showing the shell skeleton and holds it for a minimum visible period. Per-view skeleton timing was explicitly moved to follow-up #1078 and was not added here. Cached-data and refresh behavior remain governed by the existing repository loading state.

The shell/route swap uses one Vue out-in transition with a 120 ms opacity-only fade. This prevents both branches from occupying the shell simultaneously. The final scope update accepts a brief visual shift during the swap as a known limitation for follow-up #1078. Reduced-motion users receive no transition. No forced loading-shot hook remains in production, and declared shots were removed because the capture verifier rejects intentionally loading pages.

Tests cover the skeleton counts by kind, shell timing behavior, the conditional shell and RouterView transition structure, page-height layout expectations, and browser-computed normal and reduced-motion transition settings.

## Approaches tried

The first proposal was a multiple-card dashboard skeleton; review showed that it recreated the wrong board shape. It was replaced with a single dashboard block. The implementation initially tried keeping loading-state screenshot declarations, but the shot verifier treats `aria-busy` as a failed capture, so those shots were removed while component tests retained structural coverage.

Several transition structures were explored after review feedback about the shell/route handoff. The final implementation keeps one out-in transition around the loading shell and RouterView, avoids absolute positioning and overlap logic, and updates the page-height assertion to preserve the `RouterView v-else` branch. A focused browser test checks computed transition styles under both normal and reduced-motion preferences.

## Challenges and blockers

A prior handoff attempt overlapped an active check and failed during RepoOS's commit step. The final check was rerun on a stable tree. Its first remote runner hung, so RepoOS retried on another host; the retry completed successfully. The earlier failure modes around loading-state screenshots and a check-running commit were resolved by removing the loading shots and waiting for the final check to finish before requesting review.

## Key learnings

A placeholder count should describe the real page structure, not optimize for visual density. The main dashboard is a single stacked surface, so one block is a better first-load cue than a row of fake cards. Screenshot tooling may reject the exact loading state a skeleton change needs to show; tests should assert those states directly when captures are intentionally excluded. Finally, shell timing belongs at the shared shell boundary, while changes to per-view timing and more elaborate transition/layout behavior need their own scoped follow-up.
